text:
sam: Heads up — onboarding Maelstrom-7B-lite shows weird degradation after int4 conversion on long context (>2k). Short prompts fine. Suspect rotary frequency or tokenizer boundary. Anyone seen this shape before?
maria: Can you paste the inference command and a failing prompt?
sam: repro command: `python run_infer.py --model maelstrom-7b-lite --quant int4 --seq_len 4096 --prompt-file tests/long_prompts.txt`
sam: failing prompt snippet: "In a world where the river splits and the bridge is ancient, the traveler asked about the—" model completes oddly, repeats partial tokens and drops punctuation.
lee: repeating + token drop often looks like kv-cache misalignment or tokenizer emitting multi-codepoint tokens (ZWJ/diacritics). Did you compare token ids vs fp16 run?
maria: I ran a quick diff: `python utils/token_diff.py --model maelstrom --prompt tests/long_prompts.txt --mode fp16,int4` output shows index drift starting at token 1024 for some examples.
maria: paste of token diff (truncated):
``nidx fp16_id int4_id note
1018 34521 34521 ok
1019 12 12 ok
1020 0 65280 mismatch (ZWJ cluster)
1021 78 78 ok
```
art: hmm ZWJ cluster mapped to a high surrogate id in quant pipeline? Could be tokenizer normalization step being run twice in conversion. Also check rotary scaling: if head ordering changes, int4 packing can reorder bytes and break per-head rotation alignment.
sam: good point. I remembered we applied a custom tokenizer merge during conversion. I'll re-run conversion with `--no-normalize` and re-quant.
sam: quick experiment logs: 
```
# conversion v2
convert_model --input maelstrom.fp16 --tok-merge none --out tmp/mae_v2
quantize --input tmp/mae_v2 --bits 4 --packed-order headwise
INFER: seq=4096 prompt=1/10 -> ok
INFER: seq=4096 prompt=2/10 -> repeats at 2048
```
lee: still repeats at 2k, so tokenizer normalization wasn't the only factor. Can you dump rotary parameters/shape from fp16 vs quantized? Maybe head ordering got permuted.
maria: dumped shapes: `ro_pe: (12, 64, 64)` both fp16 and quantized but contents differ around head 7..12 in angle distribution.
art: run a tiny check: rotate dot-product angle histogram for heads 6..9, see if sign flip or scale mismatch. I had a similar bug once where quant packing used little-endian byte groups and our per-head dequantizer expected big-endian.
infra-bot: CI run queued: build/mae-onboard-1715 started. Logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/mae-onboard-1715
sam: I'll also run a minimal kernel test: `python tests/rotary_check.py --model tmp/mae_v2 --heads 12 --dump-head 7` to compare angle vectors. Will post diffs.
maria: if it's head permutation, candidate quickfix is to try `--packed-order interleaved` or swap head groups before quant.
sam: thanks — triaging now. If anyone has a quick script to compare tokenizer clusterization between conversions, that'd save time.
lee: I have one, will drop link: https://internal.tools/token-cluster-compare (use with auth)
sam: great. will report back with CI logs later. :thumbsup:
